concepts.title: Why Local Government: Democracy at the Doorstep

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Why Local Government: Democracy at the Doorstep' refers to.
questions.a: Local needs -- water, sanitation, street lights, schools -- are best judged where people live, so democratic theory reserves a tier of government for them. Local bodies bring government within reach: citizens can meet their representatives daily, and problems of the neighbourhood get institutions of their own.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Why Local Government: Democracy at the Doorstep'.
questions.a: The problems closest to home need governments closest to home -- democracy scales down as well as up.

concepts.title: 73rd and 74th Amendments: Constitutional Status to Local Bodies

questions.q: Explain in your own words what '73rd and 74th Amendments: Constitutional Status to Local Bodies' refers to.
questions.a: Before 1992 local bodies lived at the mercy of state governments, frequently superseded. The 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) changed that: panchayats and municipalities became constitutional institutions with regular five-year elections, reserved seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women, and State Election Commissions to conduct their polls.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about '73rd and 74th Amendments: Constitutional Status to Local Bodies'.
questions.a: From favours to rights -- the 1992 amendments made local elections mandatory, not optional.

questions.q: Under which section is '73rd and 74th Amendments: Constitutional Status to Local Bodies' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Panchayati Raj: The Three-Tier Rural Structure

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Panchayati Raj: The Three-Tier Rural Structure' refers to.
questions.a: Rural local government now runs in three tiers -- gram panchayat at village level, panchayat samiti or block level, and zilla parishad at district level -- with the gram sabha of all voters above each panchayat. The eleventh schedule lists 29 subjects, from agriculture to rural housing, that state legislatures may devolve.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Panchayati Raj: The Three-Tier Rural Structure'.
questions.a: Village to block to district -- three rungs of elected rural self-rule, capped by the assembly of all voters.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Panchayati Raj: The Three-Tier Rural Structure' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Urban Local Government and Women's Leadership

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Urban Local Government and Women's Leadership' refers to.
questions.a: The 74th Amendment mapped urban areas to municipal corporations, municipal councils and nagar panchayats by size, with ward committees below. Reservation for women -- a third of seats and chairposts -- produced over a million elected women in local bodies, the world's largest cohort of women in public office, gradually shifting gender expectations of leadership.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Urban Local Government and Women's Leadership'.
questions.a: Cities get their own elected governments; women get seats by law -- and leadership follows the seat.
